sections.prepared_remarks: Thank you, operator. Apple reporting record Q1 revenue of $124.3 billion, up 4 percent year over year. iPhone revenue of $69.1 billion driven by strong demand for iPhone 16 Pro and Pro Max models. Services revenue hit an all-time high of $24.2 billion, up 12 percent. Mac revenue of $8.7 billion with M4 chip momentum. We are investing aggressively in AI. Apple Intelligence is already delighting users and we have an unmatched roadmap ahead. Greater China revenue was $21.2 billion, with improved customer feedback and stabilizing market conditions. We're extremely proud of our performance in this dynamic environment. Our installed base of active devices crossed 2.2 billion for the first time, demonstrating the enduring loyalty of our customers.
sections.financial_highlights: Total revenue $124.3 billion, EPS $2.41, gross margin 46.2 percent. Returned over $30 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks. Operating cash flow of $32.3 billion. We exited Q1 with $66.2 billion in cash and marketable securities, net cash neutral position achieved ahead of schedule. Services gross margin expanded 80 basis points to 74.8 percent, a new record. We are seeing strong growth across App Store, AppleCare, iCloud, and advertising. Our subscription portfolio now exceeds 1 billion paid subscriptions, up from 900 million last year. We expect Q2 revenue to grow in the mid-to-high single digits year over year with continued margin expansion.
sections.qanda_session:
Samik Chatterjee: Tim, on Apple Intelligence — when do you expect a more meaningful revenue contribution from AI features specifically? And how should we think about the upgrade cycle dynamics once AI features become a bigger part of the iPhone value proposition?

Tim Cook: Samik, thanks for the question. Apple Intelligence is already driving customer satisfaction and we believe it's a meaningful upgrade driver. We are still in the early innings. The features we have rolled out with iOS 18 have been well received. As we move deeper into 2025 with more sophisticated capabilities, we expect the differentiation value to increase. We're not going to put a specific number on revenue contribution, but the upgrade cycle we're seeing in China and developed markets aligns with our thesis that AI features are accelerating trades.

Erik Woodring: Luca, can you walk us through the Services margin dynamics? It seems like the advertising and cloud businesses are growing faster than the overall Services bundle — does that mix shift continue to expand margins further?

Luca Maestri: Erik, you're right. The high-growth components of Services — particularly advertising and iCloud — carry margins above the Services average. As these grow faster than the total, they are indeed margin-accretive. We expect this dynamic to persist through fiscal 2025. Our guidance implies Services gross margin in the 74 to 76 percent range for the full year, and we see room for further expansion as the mix benefits continue.
sections.forward_outlook: Tim Cook: Looking ahead to Q2, we are optimistic. The iPhone 16 lineup is performing well globally. Vision Pro is building its developer ecosystem. We continue to see strong Enterprise iPhone deployments, particularly in financial services and healthcare. Our commitment to carbon neutrality by 2030 remains on track. We have reduced our Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by over 60 percent since 2015. We are on a clear path to making every Apple product carbon neutral by 2030, including our supply chain transition to renewable energy which is 95 percent complete. We are investing in next-generation silicon to lead on-device AI performance. The capital efficiency of our model remains exceptional — over $30 billion returned annually while funding substantial R&D.
